graph.method: function-level static graph over the exact candidate DSOs: nm-defined functions; objdump direct call edges; and an intraprocedural abstract interpreter that resolves indirect control transfers from relocations (GOT/PLT), immutable dispatch tables, relative jump tables, literal callback stores, field-offset stores in reachable code, and an interprocedural argument summary.  A site that cannot be resolved keeps its evidence class; only a site with no class admits the global address-taken union
graph.upper_bound_rule: least fixed point of a monotone transfer function (Kildall 1973; Cousot & Cousot 1977): direct edges + the resolver's per-site target sets +, for every unresolved site whose containing function is reachable, the class-independent evidence union (materialised addresses, relocated function slots including in-image GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT targets, field-store values and unresolved-call argument targets) plus the site's own targets. The union iterates until the reachable set stops growing; a class-specific set is precision reporting only and can never narrow the bound, so losing precision cannot lose reachability

analysis_identity.basis: sha256 over, in module-name order, each module name and a canonical JSON input record: every allocated (SHF_ALLOC) section's (name, ELF type, virtual address, size, sha256 of its bytes), the sorted relocation table (section, section-relative offset, type, canonical symbol, addend), the sorted [name, addr, size, kind] defined-symbol rows, the sorted dynamic-symbol rows, and the loader entries (SONAME/NEEDED/RUNPATH/RPATH). Required minimum sections: .text, .plt, .plt.got, .init, .fini, .rodata, .data, .data.rel.ro, .data.rel.ro.local, .got, .got.plt, .init_array, .fini_array; NOBITS sections (address/size only): .bss. Excluded: .debug_*, .zdebug_*, .comment, .note*, .gnu_debuglink, .gnu_debugaltlink, .gnu.build.attributes, every non-allocated section (SHF_ALLOC is absent). ``.llvm.<hash>`` and ``@@VERSION`` suffixes are canonicalised as in the symbol table; the DSO file digest is recorded as a non-identity.
analysis_identity.note: the DSO file digest is recorded as a non-identity: it changes with build paths and debug strings when the executable bytes do not. Input completeness is not proved by this digest: it binds the enumerated inputs, and a future analysis that reads another section must extend the enumeration.

closure.analysis_identity_basis: the DSO file digest is not an analysis identity: a comment-only edit changes it with byte-identical analysis sections and symbol addresses; the identity hashes every analysis-relevant section (name/type/address/size/bytes), the canonical relocation table, the defined- and dynamic-symbol tables and the loader entries, and excludes analysis-irrelevant metadata (basis string in analysis_identity.basis)

refutation_admission.rule: an exclusion derived against the pre-closure direct set that the sound upper bound reaches is false: the subject's contribution is admitted with a witness and the closure is recomputed, until no admission grows the bound (cap 4 passes; exhaustion is ADMISSION_NONCONVERGENT).  Admission may only add targets; exclusions the bound does not reach survive and remain validated

symbol_disposition_summary.rule: every symbolic value in the module residual bound and in a residual site's own bound is resolved through the fixed order exact-export, version-stripped-export, names-at, dynamic-symbol-table, soname-qualified-import, plt-stub; a symbol covered by a cited documented external interface is external-contract; every other symbol is blocking and is refused, never counted and discarded

bound_evidence_sources.rule: a residual site's bound is address_taken_union plus taken_code plus every field-store value plus every unresolved-call argument target plus the site's own resolver targets and arg_targets; it is independent of the site's class, so a precision loss can only widen it

closure.reachable_functions_sha256_rule: sha256 over the newline-terminated sorted 'module:hex_address:canonical_name' entries; the name is canonicalised (compiler .llvm.<hash> and symbol-version suffix removed) exactly as the analysis identity canonicalises its symbol rows, so a comment-only rebuild cannot move the digest
closure.reachable_functions_raw_name_sha256_rule: sha256 over the same entries with the raw nm name; it embeds the build-dependent .llvm.<hash> and is recorded as a non-identity, not as movement evidence

reachable_export_symbols.note: candidate DSO exports reached by the graph, including the 12 consumer imports; the consumer-imported set is in symbol_evidence

special_edges.provider_narrowing: the consumer imports no provider installation/selection symbol and no dynamic name lookup, and the reachable set contains 3 provider/engine selection symbol(s); provider dispatch is therefore limited to built-in providers whose tables are reached through the resolver, not to a dynamically registered provider
special_edges.note: each listed class was checked against the reachable set of the exact candidate code; an empty list is an observed absence on this closure, not an assumption.  A reachable dynamic name lookup would be an unmodelled edge class because the static graph cannot resolve names

unmapped_crate_functions.note: crate-namespace functions with no module-path mapping; they are a coverage limit of the demangler, not a claim of unreachability

observed_trace.note: no observed execution trace was supplied; the closure is the static upper bound alone

limits: inlined callees have no out-of-line function node; their code is attributed to the caller, so a source file whose only contribution is inlined has no node of its own
the resolver is an over-approximation: an unresolved site is admitted at its evidence class, and every unclassified site is listed rather than silently dropped
the residual bound is class-independent and therefore monotone, but it is still a may-bound: a function that no materialised-address source names is not admitted, so monotonicity is not completeness

the analysis identity binds the enumerated analysis inputs (sections, relocations, defined and dynamic symbol tables, loader entries); it is not a proof of input completeness: a derivation that starts reading a new section must extend the enumeration, and two candidates with identical enumerated inputs but a different unenumerated fact would collide
a dynamic trace proves execution, not unreachability, and never narrowed this graph
function-level reachability is not a proof that a site is safe; it bounds which obligations apply

precision.purpose: replace the global address-taken collapse with per-site, evidence-bound target sets; every residual site states why it remains unresolved

got_or_table.invariant: the slot's value is fixed by the dynamic loader and the slot lies in .got/.got.plt/.data.rel.ro/.rodata, which are immutable after relocation; a writable .data/.bss slot is used only with the union of all stores performed by reachable code

table.mechanism: static dispatch/vtable table read with a known base
table.invariant: the base address is a link-time constant (lea or a relocated pointer), so every entry is a relocation-resolved function address; an unfilled or open entry makes the site unresolved

switch.evidence: 4-byte relative entries from a known .rodata base
switch.invariant: the table base is a link-time constant and every entry is decoded; targets that are function starts are admitted, intra-function targets add no new node

field.evidence: stores to that offset by reachable code, consumer-imported values and the return values of consumer-imported constructors, and code-materialised addresses when the field is open
field.invariant: a function value installed in a reachable object at a known offset is either written by reachable code (store summary), supplied by the consumer (its imported symbols and their returns, since the artefact has no dynamic name lookup), or address-materialised in reachable code; an open field adds the code-materialised set

materialised.mechanism: direct call through a value with no static table provenance
materialised.evidence: address-of materialisations in reachable code + consumer imports
materialised.invariant: after GOT/table/switch/field resolution, a remaining value can only be an address taken in reachable code or a value supplied by the consumer; a site that cannot be assigned even this class is listed as unclassified and admits the global union

precision.invariants_summary: Each class is narrowed only by evidence that fixes the possible values at the site.  A trace never narrows anything.  Functions that are not observed remain reachable if any bound admits them.  The residual class is a bound, not a claim that every listed function is called.

static_table_instance.rule: field-sensitive key (object type, pointer-slot offset, member offset); the base object is the function's declared context parameter, proven through the entry register, whole-register copies or a frame spill whose every reaching store is the same parameter (branches are never unioned); the effective table type is the declared pointer-field type or a source cast of that field to a decidable repr(C) layout; every scalar store to the slot in the dispatch table's constructor cohort must write a declared static instance of that type; every member read must be an in-image function start; a partial instance set or a mutable table refuses the site rather than unioning it

semantic_store_target_bounding.rule: a slot written by reachable code is bounded by the values those writers actually store, resolved through their provenance: an in-image lea, a GLOB_DAT of a symbol defined in this image, a caller parameter chain, or one level of an object field whose slot writer is known.  Any reachable store whose provenance is not image-bounded keeps the site UNRESOLVED.  Declared symbol names are a cross-check, never the source of truth, and a declared-but-absent name cannot void the rule.

refutation_admission.rule: each row names the exclusion subject the final upper bound reaches, the targets admitted with it, and whether the admission left the site's target set finite.  A site whose admitted caller/writer has no finite recorded contribution becomes UNRESOLVED with a named refutation-unbounded property rather than keeping an unsound finite claim

precision.settled: at least one reachable unresolved site is target-bounded: its slot has no per-call-site witness for a documented ABI contract (for example an internal Rust callback), or the site has no evidence class and admits the global address-taken union

unattributed_admissions.rule: a candidate target that no caller row attributes is admitted into the upper bound and never dropped; the list is the receipt's account of those admissions

refutation_admissions.rule: an exclusion the final upper bound refutes is admitted with its witness on the record that carries it; the subject and the admitted targets are named in the record's refutation_admissions

edge_provenance.rule: every indirect site emits a semantic identity (source operation, defining function, call-site role, per-target provenance chain) plus a disposition; an address is recorded only as an artifact-local witness; every row carries a row_kind from a closed vocabulary, so `exclusions[]` holds only target drops and the auxiliary lists hold only subject claims; every target drop is bound to a structured subject-to-target mapping (candidate_source for caller-bound drops, evidence.targets for declared-name drops, writer would_store_targets for writer drops); a caller-bound drop is recomputed from candidate_source's per-call-site witnesses, and a candidate that no caller row attributes is admitted and listed in unattributed_admissions; every claim is bound to the record's own module; a chain step comes from a closed vocabulary and carries a payload
edge_provenance.refusal_rule: a row whose row_kind or reason belongs to the other list kind, a target dropped without a checkable structured mapping, a claim whose mapping disagrees with the recomputed candidate_source, an exclusion whose subject disagrees with its target or module, a claim that disagrees with a mutually redundant ledger (target_set, candidate_source, admitted_targets, derivation, disposition-derived target_reachability), a duplicate edge identity, a proved/contract record with an empty target or no defining symbol, or a reachability exclusion that contradicts the final upper bound refuses the closure with EDGE_RECORD_EXCLUSION_UNSOUND / REACHABILITY_EXCLUSION_UNSOUND

demotions.note: an empty admitted set or a missing defining symbol is a resolver gap, not a proof; those records are demoted to UNRESOLVED so the gap stays visible instead of being counted as PROVED_TARGET_SET

edge_provenance.records_path_basis: repo-relative when the sidecar is inside the repository, otherwise absolute; the default is the gitignored workdir and --edge-records is the only override

non_claims: This is a reachability measurement, not a memory-safety proof and not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion.
DISCHARGED means an existing committed receipt covers the exact site; this tool did not re-audit, re-run or independently review that receipt.
The upper bound is a function-level linked-code over-approximation, not a whole-program or source-level call graph.

Record-level validation proves internal consistency and agreement with the graph-derived final upper bound.  It does not prove that a record was produced by this analyzer rather than forged: a forged record that is internally consistent is outside its power.  Admissibility needs the identity chain in edge_provenance.admissibility (validator sha256, record schema, artefact sha256, sidecar digest and line count) and a re-run of the pinned validator over the pinned sidecar.
No crate build, test, Miri, ASan or cryptographic court was run by this tool.

The residual bound is a monotone may-bound, not a completeness proof: it cannot admit a target that no materialised-address evidence names, and the fixpoint is over the linked image plus the resolved OpenSSL DSOs, not a whole-program call graph.
The analysis identity is over .text and the symbol table.  It is not a byte-for-byte reproducibility claim across toolchains and it does not cover data-section contents.
The dynamic-trace axis is absent unless a trace is supplied; its absence is recorded, not treated as evidence.
